Government Impersonation

Council Housing Scam UK: Spot a Fake Housing Offer

Council housing is allocated under the local council's rules and housing-need system; an outsider cannot sell you priority or guarantee an offer.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-06-21 · Updated 2026-07-10 · 2 min read

council housing scam UKfake council housing offerhousing benefit scamlocal authority housing fraudcouncil house application scam
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Report it — call Report Fraud on 0300 123 2040 (Police Scotland: 101), and forward scam texts to 7726.

What the scam looks like

Someone poses as housing staff or claims to have contacts inside a council and offers a property, priority or a “fast-tracked” application for an upfront payment. Contact may arrive by social media, messaging app, phone or email. The channel alone does not prove fraud, but a demand for money to manipulate the housing list is outside the published allocation process.

How council housing applications work

GOV.UK says applicants apply through their local council. Each council has its own rules; applicants usually join a list and are not guaranteed a property. Councils allocate homes using points or bands based on housing need. In choice-based schemes, applying for an advertised property is often called “bidding”, but GOV.UK explicitly notes that this bidding does not involve money.

Avoid the unsupported blanket claim that no council can ever charge any housing-related fee in any circumstances. The accurate red flag is a payment requested in exchange for priority, fabricated eligibility or a guaranteed council home. Verify any other charge directly with the council.

Warning signs

  • Payment is requested to move you up the list or guarantee a home.
  • The person asks for false documents or information to alter your assessed need.
  • You are pressured to pay before independently contacting the council.
  • The offer cannot be found in your official housing account or confirmed by the council.

Verify an offer

Contact the council using the details on its official website, not details supplied by the person making the offer. Ask the housing team to confirm the application, bidding record and property. Do not pay or provide documents until the council has confirmed the contact.

Illegal subletting is a separate issue

A genuine social-housing tenant may also unlawfully sublet a property. In England and Wales, the Prevention of Social Housing Fraud Act 2013 created offences relating to certain unlawful subletting. The dishonest offence can carry up to two years' imprisonment, and courts can make unlawful-profit orders. The Act does not extend to Scotland or Northern Ireland, so do not present that penalty as a single UK-wide rule.

If money was paid

Contact the bank immediately and tell the council. Preserve the profile, listing, messages and payment details. Report the profile to the platform on which it appeared.

Reporting in the UK

Report a fake housing offer to the relevant local council. If money was lost, report the crime to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland; in Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101. Suspected tenancy fraud can usually be reported through the council's own fraud-reporting service.

Frequently asked questions

Can someone guarantee me a council home for a payment?

No one outside the council's allocation process can sell a guaranteed offer or priority. Confirm every offer directly with the council.

Does “bidding” for council housing mean paying money?

No. In a choice-based lettings scheme, “bidding” means expressing interest in a property; GOV.UK says it does not involve money.
